newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu's sacked nanny sues for back pay.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu's sacked nanny sues for back pay.

text.p: Benjamin Netanyahu's disgruntled ex-nanny, fired last July after scorching soup, is suing the Israeli prime minister and first lady for more than $36,000 in back pay, her attorney said on Thursday.

The South African-born Tanya Shaw, 21, said in a petition to a Jerusalem labour court that Netanyahu and his wife Sara failed to pay extra wages for overtime and for work on the sabbath during her six months of employment, as required by law.
"The overtime and sabbath wages along with interest amount to 120,000 shekels ($36,363) to date," Shaw's attorney Moshe Zingel told Reuters.
He said the judge at the opening hearing ordered the Netanyahus to respond to the petition within 45 days. Zingel said Sara Netanyahu would probably have to take the witness stand.

"I have nothing against Sara Netanyahu personally...the fact is that Sara owes me money for hours that I've worked in her house looking after her children and I should be paid that money." Shaw told Israel television.
Zingel said Shaw's name had been tarnished by the affair and as a result she had been unable to land another job.

Shaw told reporters in several interviews after her dismissal in July that the first lady was obsessed with cleanliness, had called her "a murderer" and tossed her out for burning soup in the kitchen.
The scandal remained on the front pages of Israeli tabloids for days, embarrassing Netanyahu just one month after his election.
